recognize_zh: 血片中許多紅血球邊緣像被咬掉一口（bite cells/degmacytes），另有血紅素偏向一側、另一側透明的水泡細胞與偏心紅血球（blister cells、eccentrocytes），符合氧化性溶血，例如給予 rasburicase 後誘發 G6PD 缺乏症溶血。
features: Numerous bite cells with semicircular peripheral defects in the red cell membrane
Blister cells/eccentrocytes with hemoglobin displaced to one side and a clear membrane-bound area
Scattered dense, irregularly contracted red cells and occasional spherocytic forms
Normocytic red cells overall; platelets present in normal numbers
No schistocytes or red cell agglutination
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous red cells with sharply demarcated peripheral bites (degmacytes) and blister cells with hemoglobin retracted to one side leaving a clear rim, along with dense contracted cells and occasional spherocytic forms. Platelets are adequate and there are no schistocytes. Findings are consistent with oxidative hemolysis; in a patient treated with an oxidant drug such as rasburicase, they are suggestive of G6PD deficiency, and G6PD activity should be measured (ideally after reticulocytosis subsides) with methemoglobin assessment.

ddx.vs: Schistocytes are small angular fragments and helmet cells with thrombocytopenia, rather than intact cells with rounded bites or eccentric hemoglobin.
Shows spherocytes, polychromasia and a positive DAT without bite or blister cells.
Produces similar bite cells and Heinz bodies but with normal G6PD activity and positive hemoglobin instability testing.

ddx.dx: Dapsone or other drug-induced oxidant injury in G6PD-normal patients
ddx.vs: Morphology is identical, so G6PD assay and drug dose history are needed to separate them.
